patterns.title: Declaration and definition chronology can change GC/1.3.2 output
patterns.summary: Moving file-scope definitions earlier can change one-pass visibility, register allocation, section extents, and relocations even when the C declarations appear equivalent.
patterns.conditions: Apply as a compiler-wide diagnostic under GC/1.3.2; probe each owner locally because stage.c is a counterexample to the mdparty tail-definition requirement.

source_condition.change: Move file-scope object definitions earlier or otherwise alter declaration/definition chronology while retaining nominally equivalent declarations.
requires: same compiler version and flags
same symbol ownership and types
before/after object and relocation comparison

possible_changes: whether a nested helper operation remains a call when the enclosing helper is later auto-inlined
known_signatures: a semantics-preserving reorder regresses many exact functions
section extent changes without an intentional data-layout change
a standalone helper compiled with prototype-only visibility remains call-bearing inside a later exact auto-inline expansion
complete copied bodies and absent call relocations prove a depth-two inline chain whose result changes when one definition moves

patterns.rule: Treat declaration chronology as a testable compiler variable; do not modernize definition placement or copy a tail-definition layout without owner-local proof.
safe_actions: make a bounded owner-local chronology probe
compare every independently exact function and affected data section
record both positive and negative owner results

patterns.conditions: Use as a compiler-wide diagnostic; local prototypes or narrower owner-local headers are acceptable only when symbol authority and an owner-specific visibility probe support them.

source_condition.change: Replace the target-visible include closure or local prototypes with a broader header that exposes additional declarations, macros, inline bodies, or header-owned data.
requires: authoritative signatures remain semantically compatible
the include changes the visible declaration, macro, inline-body, or local-data set
before-and-after object, relocation, and retained-section comparison

possible_changes: header-owned literal or local-static section prefixes
known_signatures: one exact caller becomes eight bytes shorter
several independently exact functions diverge after a header-only cleanup
a local macro changes an external call relocation to an internal helper
a header implementation adds target-absent local constants to `.sdata2`

patterns.rule: Do not treat broader modern header visibility as historically authentic merely because its declarations and semantics are correct; reproduce and test the retail translation-unit declaration, macro, inline-body, and local-data visibility.
safe_actions: compare the complete preprocessed declaration and macro set before and after the include
run an owner-local broad-header probe
compare call relocations and raw retained data prefixes
retain narrow local declarations or owner-local header selection only with symbol authority and recorded evidence

patterns.title: Check helper boundaries and object lifetimes before adding code-generation controls
patterns.summary: Real helper boundaries, automatic inline decisions, narrow contracts, and block-scoped lifetimes can explain repeated register and control-flow mismatches across related callers.
patterns.conditions: Use when the same mismatch family appears around calls, saved registers, temporary elimination, or nested control flow; a single isolated match is insufficient.

source_condition.change: Flatten or recreate helpers, widen a narrow contract, or move a temporary outside its likely original block scope.
requires: a repeated mismatch family across related call sites
target or sibling evidence for the helper or contract

known_signatures: multiple callers close together after restoring one helper family
a block-scope or signed-contract correction removes one repeated temporary

patterns.rule: Before using pragmas or artificial expressions, test the authenticated helper boundary, narrow type contract, and block lifetime that could naturally produce the mismatch family.
safe_actions: compare the same helper pattern across all known callers
test signedness and scope independently
retain the change only when related callers improve without exact regressions

source_condition.change: Widen an s16 argument or return contract to int, or insert casts that erase the original signed-short node.
requires: target load/store or extension evidence
caller and consumer width review

known_signatures: an exact body closes only after restoring an s16 return
multiple inline boundaries share the same signed argument-node difference

patterns.rule: Choose narrow signed types from target and consumer evidence, not from modern convenience or one function's isolated code generation.
safe_actions: inspect caller and consumer widths before changing the signature
compare extension instructions at every boundary
re-test all Matching consumers of a shared declaration

patterns.conditions: Apply whenever source, headers, symbols, catalogs, or configuration are consulted from an independent repository for the same retail target.

matching target region or consumer contract
current-toolchain object and relocation validation for emitted code

a retained source blob is labeled Matching without committed object or relocation proof

extract only the contract or source hypothesis needed by the active owner

patterns.title: Use sibling binary parity as a boundary check, not source provenance
patterns.summary: A matching MP4, MP5, or MP7 retail binary can independently corroborate an MP6 instruction pattern, layout boundary, or access sequence, but a binary supplies no original C tokens and cannot authenticate a source expression, helper boundary, local lifetime, or semantic name.
patterns.conditions: Apply when another shipped Mario Party binary shares code or data with MP6 but no pinned matching source blob authenticates the candidate source form.

source_condition.change: Promote a sibling-binary match from corroborating target evidence to original-source authority.
requires: pinned sibling game, region, binary, address, and compared byte range
independent MP6 instruction, relocation, data, or consumer proof
separate source provenance before asserting C spelling or semantic names

possible_changes: higher confidence in a machine-level control or access pattern
a bounded layout or owner-shape cross-check
no additional confidence in source tokens or compiler-generated temporary structure
known_signatures: MP7 reproduces an MP6 instruction stream or stack rotation but no source donor exists
matching MP5 source and MP7 binary parity agree, while MP6 target evidence still decides the retained adaptation
a same-binary map supplies names only and no recoverable source body

patterns.rule: Record sibling retail parity as independent binary evidence. Do not file it under same-game independent source provenance, and do not use it alone to claim source spelling, helper extraction, local temporaries, or semantic names.
safe_actions: record the exact sibling binary range and the MP6 dimension it corroborates
use parity to bound control flow, access widths, stack shape, or layout
require a pinned source blob or direct MP6 compiler recovery before asserting source form
retain fn_/lbl_ or established names when parity is the only naming evidence
examples: MP7 parity corroborated the GSSDK gender session/reset access pattern, while MP6 target recovery supplied the source and types.
MP7 parity corroborated several board and speech-owner machine-level shapes alongside independent MP6 consumer evidence.
counterexamples: MP7 reproduced board/audio's four-local stack rotation, but no authenticated expression recreated the compiler-generated first temporary, so no synthetic helper or register-forcing source was admitted.
A same-binary symbol map can suggest a name but is not a source donor.

patterns.title: Mine cross-owner analogues by ordered relocation skeleton, then rebind target ownership
patterns.summary: Thirty-nine mdsingdll functions totaling 7424 text bytes and 465 physical relocations became independently exact from mdpartydll analogue clusters when candidates were selected by ordered calls and relocations, rebound to target-owned symbols and types, and verified as consumed generated objects through the retail REL. Exact perimeter functions remain independently valuable when an interior analogue is blocked by inline chronology, scheduling, or compiler-owned conversion pools.
patterns.conditions: Apply when an eligible non-board, non-minigame target has unclaimed functions and authenticated same-game source from another owner contains a compatible ordered external-call and relocation skeleton.

source_condition.change: Use a same-game function from a different owner as a natural-C hypothesis for one or more unclaimed target functions.
requires: stable donor and target identities
compatible ABI and ordered call or symbol-relocation skeleton
target-side proof for globals, callbacks, types, literals, and counts
explicit target split and generated matching-object consumption

possible_changes: multiple exact target functions from one coherent source family
correct call order and relocation ownership before local expression tuning
shared target declarations across a contiguous recovery cluster
false positives when only a common API set or semantic resemblance is compared
known_signatures: donor and target share the same ordered engine calls and compatible branch or loop shape
target relocations bind analogous calls to different owner-local globals or callbacks
several donor and target stable IDs share one address delta plus a consistent named-global and named-constant translation
a new split appears configured but generated Ninja or link inputs still consume retail fallback

patterns.rule: Treat cross-owner same-game source as a ranked hypothesis generator: fingerprint ordered relocations and control shape, cluster compatible targets, rebind every contract from target evidence, and retain only subsets with exact instructions, relocations, generated-object consumption, consumers, and retail replay. After bounded probes, keep dependency-closed exact perimeter functions and revert pool-, scheduling-, or inline-blocked interiors instead of discarding the whole cluster.
safe_actions: catalog eligible donor stable IDs with ordered external-call and symbol-relocation signatures
rank unclaimed targets by exact skeleton before looser API overlap
batch contiguous or shared-declaration candidates into one bounded multi-function compile probe
retain independently exact subsets and record compact negative fingerprints for rejected candidates
split an exact dependency-closed perimeter away from a blocked interior when target order and generated ownership remain provable
verify build.ninja and link inputs consume the generated object before accepting configured status

patterns.title: Triangulate configured extent and public consumers before retaining an opaque overlay
patterns.summary: Independent staffdll and mdbankdll recoveries replaced misleading offset-only or first-word interpretations with natural aggregates after configured sizes, public field/stride types, callbacks, and state consumers were triangulated; exact text and relocations were preserved across both compiler profiles.
patterns.conditions: Apply when an untyped target address or offset can be reproduced by an opaque overlay, pointer slot, or multiple plausible public aggregate fields.

source_condition.change: Choose a natural aggregate owner and typed field chain instead of retaining an offset-only overlay or first-word pointer interpretation.
requires: configured symbol extent or independently bounded allocation size
typed offsets and strides from public or authenticated owner contracts
multiple independent read, write, callback, teardown, or state consumers
exact instructions, relocations, and retained consumers

possible_changes: natural field offsets and array strides
removal of opaque casts or overlays without byte changes
different relocation ownership when the first word was misclassified as a pointer slot
known_signatures: one address is repeatedly loaded through several typed offsets larger than a pointer
configured size divided by repeated consumer count yields a stable natural element stride
a public hookData or owner field leads through public structs to the target offset
an opaque overlay matches bytes but conflicts with callback, teardown, or mutation consumers

patterns.rule: Treat an offset match as a lead, not ownership proof. Before keeping an overlay or pointer-slot type, triangulate configured extent, public field and stride contracts, and every independent consumer; retain the narrowest natural aggregate that makes those dimensions and exact relocations agree.
safe_actions: list every configured extent and target relocation touching the candidate owner
trace public consumer types through the complete pointer and field chain
divide total extent by authenticated repeated-consumer count to test natural element stride
verify callbacks, initialization, mutation, and teardown against the same owner
remove temporary overlays once a public natural contract reproduces identical bytes
examples: staffdll public HU3D_MODEL.hookData through HU3D_PARTICLE/HU3D_PARTICLE_DATA replaced temporary offset overlays while preserving 25 exact functions, 0x9BC text, and 125 physical relocations.
mdbankdll configured lbl_1_bss_1998 size 0x50 plus camera callbacks/state consumers authenticated one owner aggregate and added twelve exact functions, 1396 bytes, and 94 physical relocations.
mdbankdll configured extents divided by repeated consumer counts authenticated eight additional owner arrays and closed fn_1_1994/fn_1_5550 for 1312 bytes.
main:game/mgdata replaced a byte-oriented 83-record overlay with natural MGDATA dimensions after archive catalogs, access widths, and five exact consumer owners agreed.

REL:mdpartydll:mdparty recovered 17 logical sprite-group counts, 58 typed descriptors, 67 HuVecF positions, and an 11-entry signed selection graph from target extents and independent consumers without inventing padding fields.

Waves 31-37 recover GSSDK state, handle, serialized-data, table, and signal-processing layouts only where MP6 allocation sizes, access widths, callbacks, relocations, or public consumers independently bound them.
wave 72 retained two adjacent 16-entry effect arrays because MP6 deliberately indexes 32 entries from the first; consumer behavior proved adjacency without inventing a combined declaration.
counterexamples: Matching one field offset does not authenticate the semantic field or containing type.
Repeated high/low address materialization of the first word does not prove pointer-to-pointer ownership.
Do not keep an opaque overlay after a public consumer chain reproduces the layout naturally.

patterns.title: Use authenticated fixed arity to choose direct calls or a bounded workspace
patterns.summary: A five-entry miraclebook resource catalog authenticated an exact direct-call sequence where a loop emitted 40 extra bytes, while a 16-entry s01 motion catalog authenticated an exact local permutation workspace where destructive pseudo-swaps failed. Fixed arity narrows natural source shape but does not prescribe one universal form.
patterns.conditions: Apply when catalog, configured extent, or complete consumers authenticate a small fixed resource count and an otherwise natural loop, unrolled sequence, or shuffle differs structurally from target code.

source_condition.change: Express a catalog-proven fixed operation as direct calls or a bounded local ordering workspace according to target instruction shape.
requires: authenticated fixed count and resource order domain
target control flow distinguishing loop control from direct calls
target index/load/store lifetime distinguishing a workspace from destructive table mutation
exact instructions, relocations, and consumers

possible_changes: removal of loop-control instructions for a small explicit call sequence
preservation of bounded index and shuffle lifetimes through a local permutation array
large structural drift when the wrong fixed-arity form is selected
known_signatures: target repeats a small call sequence with no induction variable or back edge
target retains bounded local index loads and stores around a randomized ordering
a loop is exact in calls but larger by only loop-control bytes
destructive pseudo-swaps lose a target local-workspace lifetime

patterns.rule: After authenticating a small fixed count, use target control and data-flow shape to choose a natural explicit call sequence or bounded local workspace. Test the coherent family once; never force unrolling, invent a table, or mutate shared data merely to remove a loop.
safe_actions: pin the count from catalog, configured extent, or complete consumers
compare ordered calls, induction/back-edge instructions, and local index loads/stores
cluster the complete small fixed family in one source hypothesis
retain only exact subsets and revert destructive pseudo-swap or invented-table probes
examples: miraclebookdll fn_1_7998 became strict exact at 4212 bytes with five catalog-authenticated direct resource calls; the loop retained 40 target-absent bytes.
s01Dll fn_1_AFC became strict exact at 0x13C bytes with a natural 16-entry motion-order workspace; destructive pseudo-swaps scored 54.632910%.
counterexamples: A constant count inferred only from one loop bound does not authenticate a resource catalog or order domain.
Fixed arity is not permission to add unroll pragmas, duplicate side effects, fabricate arrays, or hard-code unproven literals.
Use a direct sequence only when target loop control is absent; use a workspace only when target index and store chronology proves it.

patterns.title: A configured Matching label is a claim until retail proof is replayed
patterns.summary: The pinned same-game repository labels 54 owners Matching but commits no object reports, relocation reports, or replayable checksum proof; current acceptance must regenerate those dimensions.
patterns.conditions: Apply to imported status labels, historical progress reports, cached objdiff output, and source blobs from any branch or repository.

source_condition.change: Treat a historical Matching or Equivalent label as sufficient evidence for current integration.
requires: fresh active-object build
instruction and relocation comparison
section ownership comparison
standalone and every retained inline-consumer replay for shared helper source
linked retail checksum when integration is claimed

possible_changes: regression in an exact standalone body or sibling inline expansion
known_signatures: source blobs differ while both repositories label an owner Matching
no reproducible object or checksum artifact accompanies the label
one near-exact inline clone improves while an already exact helper or sibling clone changes

patterns.rule: Report configured status separately from freshly replayed retained-object, relocation, section, consumer-context, and linked-output results. A shared helper source is exact only when its standalone body and every retained inline expansion remain exact.
safe_actions: compile the active object in an isolated current worktree
save a fresh relocation-aware objdiff report
diff every exact standalone and inline context reached by an edited helper
run the serialized linked hash gate before integration completion

patterns.title: Resolve the final compiler profile from the emitted TU command
patterns.summary: MP6 uses multiple MWCC versions and layered flag profiles; the same nominal compiler family can emit under different terminal optimization, pooling, small-data, ABI, contraction, and string settings. DTK may synthesize extracted-object .comment metadata from the split configuration, so that diagnostic field is not an independent compiler fingerprint.
patterns.conditions: Apply before source-shape tuning, donor comparison, or any claim that a compiler probe represents retail.

source_condition.change: Infer a translation unit's effective compiler flags from a base profile, sibling owner, or earlier duplicate option instead of its final generated command.
requires: exact owner and object class
generated command with later options resolved
compiler and linker executable hashes
target instruction, size, relocation, and final-container fingerprints independent of extracted .comment metadata

known_signatures: O0 and O4 controls change vector helpers from compact inlined bodies to much larger output
GC/1.3.2 REL owners require sdata, sdata2, and pool controls absent from game owners
DTK reports the compiler comment configured for a split even when target-led instruction fingerprints select another compiler
one compiler family changes prologues or indirect-call shape while another reproduces the retained owner bytes
disabling floating-point contraction preserves separate target multiply/add instructions

patterns.rule: Pin and report compiler bundle, executable hash, owner class, complete generated command, final duplicate-option semantics, linker, and region before interpreting a source mismatch. Treat DTK-generated .comment as diagnostic only; the final generated command and target/output fingerprints decide the effective profile.
safe_actions: inspect the exact Ninja command for the active object
run one untouched-source compiler control when the brief and generated command conflict
compare characteristic prologues, call lowering, instruction contraction, sizes, and relocations across bounded profile controls
reject a compiler profile that regresses independently exact functions
confirm the selected profile with the linked retail gate
examples: GC/2.6 game
GC/1.3.2 standard REL
GC/1.2.5n Dolphin SDK
counterexamples: wave 21 explicitly rejects reading GC/1.3 from the target object's unlinked .comment; the selection is established by emitted owner bytes and the linked-container gate.
wave 31 shows DTK synthesizing .comment from split configuration, so inherited GC/2.6 metadata could not override the GC/1.2.5n prologue and indirect-call fingerprint.
wave 54's metadata-motivated EXIBios GC/2.6 probe expanded .text from 0x2100 to 0x3BA0, added 150 relocations, lost eleven pairings, and made nothing exact.

patterns.summary: GXInitLightAttnA and GXInitLightAttnK resolve to the same MP6 target address, proving ABI aliasing but not which SDK spelling appeared in the original source.
patterns.conditions: Apply when maps, symbol files, headers, or sibling repositories expose multiple names for one target address.

source_condition.change: Rename a call, export, global, or field solely because another same-address alias emits identical code.
requires: stable target address
prototype and call-contract agreement
independent naming provenance for source spelling

known_signatures: two SDK names relocate to main:0x800B392C
binary equality cannot distinguish the source token

patterns.rule: Preserve the established exported/API spelling unless maps, exports, SDK provenance, or stronger same-game evidence authenticates the alternative; record byte equality and naming confidence separately.
safe_actions: retain owner plus address as the stable identity
verify both aliases have the same prototype and relocation target
record alternate names as aliases rather than silently renaming source

patterns.title: Use same-game headers for ABI widths without inheriting unproved semantic names
patterns.summary: Independent MP6 headers and Matching-owner consumers provide strong width, callback, array-dimension, and offset evidence even when alternate field and function names disagree.
patterns.conditions: Use when reconstructing prototypes, callback classes, struct layouts, array extents, or compact state fields from same-game retained headers.

source_condition.change: Adopt a same-game header contract or semantic field name into an active owner.
requires: target access width and offset checks
caller and consumer ABI review
separate naming provenance

known_signatures: charman headers expose s16, u8, GX callback, and GW_CHARA_MAX contracts
different GW_PLAYER bitfield names retain the same byte offsets and widths

patterns.title: MWCC .rodata is a single region in strict creation order, not named objects then a literal pool
patterns.summary: At -O0 the object's .rodata is one region emitted in strict creation order. Named const objects and pooled literals interleave freely; there is no named-objects-first region and no dedup between a named object and an equal pool literal, though pool literals do dedup against each other. What differs between constructs is only WHEN a constant is created: a named object at its definition point (whether or not anything references it), an expression literal at the codegen of the referencing function, a static inline body's constants at its FIRST EXPANSION, and an extern-inline function-local static under '#pragma cplusplus on' at PARSE of the inline body even when never called. Only an uncalled static inline emits nothing.

patterns.title: Parentheses, register, const and compound assignment are -O0 no-ops; only real regrouping moves temporaries
patterns.summary: Under the measured GC/2.7 -O0 controls, redundant parentheses, the register storage class, const on parameters and locals, and compound assignment are codegen no-ops, and so are declared-but-never-referenced locals. Float temporaries are numbered by expression-tree shape rather than liveness, so only a genuine operator or tree-shape change moves code generation. Equality-operand reversal was also measured neutral in two GC/2.6 board/audio campaigns. A helper's definition position and an arithmetic rewrite such as division to reciprocal multiplication are NOT cosmetic forms.
patterns.conditions: Apply before spending a search budget on cosmetic source variations, or when a same-operand different-destination-register difference needs explaining.

the same destinations with swapped fmuls A/C operand fields when a commutative operand pair is reversed
different load or operand order when division by 2 is rewritten as multiplication by 0.5

patterns.title: When only stack-slot numbers remain, the lever is an inline expansion, not a nested block
patterns.summary: A bounded diagnostic for a function whose instructions are all correct but whose r1 displacements are wrong. Locals are slotted in declaration order, descending, with compiler temporaries interleaved at their point of use. An inline expansion instead allocates the inlinee's locals ascending from the bottom of the frame, below everything the caller allocates, so a group of target locals sitting underneath the compiler temporaries indicates a static inline helper - that direction is carried from the campaign, not measured here. What is measured here: declaration order inside the helper is load-bearing when the declarations are independent, a helper must be defined above its caller to be auto-expanded at all, and passing a caller value by pointer is cheaper than by value.
patterns.conditions: Apply only when structural insert/delete differences are already zero and every remaining difference is a stack-slot number or an inlinee register assignment.

source_condition.change: Extract repeated code into a static inline helper, reorder an inline helper's locals, or change how a caller value reaches the inlinee.
requires: structural differences already driven to zero
every r1 displacement dumped from both instruction streams and diffed
the inlinee's own declaration order treated as significant
byte comparison of the candidate object, not a match percentage

possible_changes: a whole group of stack slots moving together to the bottom of the frame
changed register or slot assignment inside the expansion from reordering the helper's locals
extra stores at expansion entry, and a shifted frame, when a value is passed by value
a two-level local group when one helper's call is nested inside another
known_signatures: probes p6d/p6e differ only in the declaration order of the helper's two INDEPENDENT locals: .text 152 bytes on both sides but three allocation fields differ, f28 and f29 exchanged (fmuls f28,f31,f30 -> f29,f31,f30; fadds f29,f0,f30 -> f28,f0,f30; fmuls f27,f28,f29 -> f27,f29,f28)

probes p6a/p6b are the boundary case: when the helper's second local DEPENDS on the first, exchanging the declarations is byte-identical at 140 bytes, so this lever only bites on independent declarations
probes p6a/p6c: by-pointer 140 bytes against by-value-plus-out-pointer 164 bytes; p6c also adds a term, so 24 bytes is an upper bound on the by-value cost rather than an isolated measurement
probes p8a/p8b: a helper defined above the caller is auto-expanded (.text 148) while the same helper defined below behind a prototype is called (.text 112), and .rodata order reverses with it

Treat as unverified.

patterns.rule: Once structural differences are zero and only slot numbers remain, reach for a static inline helper rather than a nested block, define it above its caller so -inline auto can expand it, pass caller-frame values by pointer, and treat the helper's declaration order as part of its identity when its locals are independent. Two such helpers differing only in declaration order are different functions and must not be merged.
safe_actions: dump and diff every r1 displacement from both streams before editing
extract repeats as static inline helpers taking parameters rather than copying arguments into locals
nest one helper call inside another to reproduce a two-level local group
pass a value the caller must keep by pointer, which MWCC folds into an r1 displacement at no instruction cost
examples: probes p6d/p6e: exchanging two independent declarations inside the helper moves three allocation fields at identical size, so the helper's declaration order is part of its identity
probes p8a/p8b: the same helper is expanded or called purely on whether its definition precedes the caller

CAMPAIGN, NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE: w01Dll fn_1_13CC closed on this lever after 361 declaration-order permutations and 719 inner-block permutations had failed, and passing one value by pointer put it at frame offset 0xa8 with two other locals pushed down. Treat as unverified.
counterexamples: The lever does not always bite: probes p6a/p6b exchange the helper's two declarations and emit byte-identical code, because the second local depends on the first. Only INDEPENDENT declarations reorder the allocation, so a null result here does not refute the inline hypothesis.
Defining the helper below its caller silently removes the lever entirely - it is then a real call, not an expansion (probes p8a/p8b). Check visibility before concluding the helper shape is wrong.
Passing the value by value instead of by pointer adds work at expansion entry and shifts the frame (probes p6a/p6c, 140 against 164 bytes).

CAMPAIGN, NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE: plain nested blocks were reported unable to produce the layout - a nested block's locals continue the enclosing block's descending run - and nesting made w01Dll worse in every ordering tried (46 -> 49..81). Treat as unverified.
The ascending-from-frame-bottom direction is carried from the w01Dll campaign and was not re-measured in the small probes here, where the inlinee's locals were enregistered rather than stack-homed.

patterns.title: Keep compound assignments inside the consuming condition when the target reuses the updated value
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, a compound or result assignment written inside its consuming condition can keep the produced value live through the store and comparison; separating the assignment may add a reload, grow the function, or rotate saved registers.
patterns.conditions: Use when target instructions store an updated or returned value and immediately compare that same value, while an otherwise natural separated assignment differs only by a reload, size change, or register-lifetime cycle.

source_condition.change: Restore one target-backed compound/result assignment to the condition that immediately consumes it.
requires: identical source semantics for the combined and separated forms
target instruction order proving immediate store and comparison
one bounded separated-versus-combined compiler control
exact relocations and no regression of exact owner neighbors

possible_changes: reuse of the updated FPR across a store and comparison
collapse of a saved-register lifetime cycle around an assigned call result
known_signatures: separated `x += step; if (x > limit)` reloads x while `(x += step) > limit` compares the produced value
the separated float form is four bytes larger than the target
an assigned call result written inside `if` removes a multi-register color cycle without changing calls or relocations
matching sibling functions repeat the compound-assignment condition naturally

patterns.rule: Test the natural assignment-consuming condition as one bounded source-shape variable when target order proves the lifetime; retain it only with exact text, relocations, and consumers, and never replace unrelated control flow with comma expressions or assignment side effects solely to shape registers.
safe_actions: compare separated and compound forms once under the exact compiler profile
verify the target store precedes the immediate comparison
look for exact same-owner or same-game compound-assignment siblings
preserve ordinary separated statements when the target reloads or the condition is not the immediate consumer

counterexamples: A semantically equivalent assignment form is not evidence unless the target store/compare or result lifetime agrees.
Do not introduce comma expressions, duplicate side effects, or assignment conditions solely to force registers.
Folded assignment conditions that are byte-neutral or worse should be reverted and recorded as negative evidence.

patterns.title: Use natural local declaration order and first use to resolve saved-register cycles
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, adjacent same-width or pointer locals can receive different saved registers when their natural declaration order, initialization point, or first semantic use changes, even when control flow, types, size, and relocations are otherwise identical. MWCC's stack allocator orders spilled locals by size class then declaration list, while graph coloring selects the lowest available register, so a pure cycle is evidence of an earlier lifetime/AST difference rather than authority to force a register.
patterns.conditions: Use only for an exact-sized function whose remaining differences form a small same-width saved-register cycle after structural control flow, owner types, calls, and relocations already agree.

source_condition.change: Restore the target-backed declaration order, initialization point, and first semantic use of adjacent natural locals.
requires: authenticated local types and ownership
exact function size and structural instruction sequence
a bounded declaration-order, initialization-point, or first-use control
exact relocations and zero regression of exact owner neighbors

possible_changes: a later saved-register lifetime when declaration and assignment are separated naturally
operand-field changes without instruction insertion or deletion
unchanged frame size, calls, and relocation stream
no emitted change when first-use chronology dominates the declarations

sequential same-type loop locals occupy descending saved registers in declaration/first-use order
an exact-sized function retains only a two- or three-register ARG cycle
a declaration initializer begins an owner-pointer lifetime before a target cleanup call cluster
legal scope or declaration movement is byte-neutral when it does not change first use
two exact-sized functions close after declaration-order changes remove complete inverse four- and eight-operand saved-register cycles

patterns.rule: Test one natural adjacent-local declaration order, one target-backed initialization point, and one independently justified first-use chronology when the mismatch is a pure saved-register cycle. Treat those as separate variables. Retain the form only when typed semantics, complete text, relocations, and consumers are exact; if the bounded controls are neutral or leave a cycle, stop and record negative evidence rather than adding register-shaping locals.
safe_actions: authenticate widths and pointer depth before changing order
compare declaration order, initialization point, and first semantic use as separate variables
separate declaration from assignment only when target calls or stores prove the later lifetime boundary
verify that no extsh, clrlwi, spill, frame, call, or relocation debt appears

patterns.title: Use chained assignment when one RHS value feeds target-ordered stores
patterns.summary: Repeated MWCC O0 recoveries show that a natural chained assignment can evaluate one authenticated right-hand value once and emit several stores in the target's right-to-left lvalue order, while equivalent independent statements can duplicate a load or immediate and change stack or reload chronology.
patterns.conditions: Use only when target instructions prove one RHS evaluation or load, multiple stores of that value, and a specific store order that independent statements fail to reproduce.

source_condition.change: Express several assignments from one authenticated side-effect-free value as one chained assignment rather than independent statements.
requires: identical assignment semantics and destination types
target evidence for one RHS evaluation and every destination store
target-backed right-to-left store chronology
one bounded chained-versus-independent compiler control
exact instructions, relocations, and consumers after the change

possible_changes: one shared immediate, call result, or interpolated value
removal of a duplicate load or immediate
different stack-object lifetime and reload placement
known_signatures: the target loads one constant once and stores it to adjacent fields in reverse textual destination order
independent statements emit a second li or reload and grow the function
a chained call-result assignment stores two vector components before one target reload
a chained interpolated-value assignment restores both stack layout and component store order

patterns.rule: When the target proves one side-effect-free RHS value feeding several ordered stores, test one natural chained assignment against independent statements. Retain it only when complete text, relocations, and consumers become exact; never chain unrelated side effects, calls with ambiguous evaluation order, or assignments with different conversion semantics merely to shape registers.
safe_actions: confirm the RHS is evaluated once in the target
compare destination store order and conversion widths
measure one independent-statement control under the pinned owner profile
reject the chain if it changes side-effect order, narrowing, volatile access, or consumer semantics

Do not use a chain when destination conversions differ or the target evaluates the RHS more than once.

patterns.title: Test pointer truthiness or literal zero when typed NULL materializes a compare operand
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, a natural pointer truth test or comparison with integer literal 0 can lower to a direct cmplwi, while an equivalent comparison with typed NULL can materialize zero in a register and emit li plus cmplw. An authenticated integer typedef that carries an address can require a consumer-local pointer cast for the reverse transition without changing its public ABI.
patterns.conditions: Use when the target directly compares a proven pointer against immediate zero but the candidate materializes a null operand, when the candidate is exactly four bytes larger for that reason, or when target and independent address-semantics evidence prove that an address-valued integer handle is consumed in the pointer-null domain.

source_condition.change: Select the authenticated integer-zero or pointer-null expression domain for one null guard without changing the producer's public type.
requires: the expression is authenticated as a pointer or as an integer typedef carrying an address
identical null-test semantics
target and candidate compare instructions
exact control flow, relocations, and consumers after the change
independent sibling/header address semantics before casting an integer typedef

possible_changes: removal of li r0,0 plus cmplw
introduction of the target li r0,0 plus cmplw for an authenticated address-handle consumer
unchanged branch structure and relocation stream
known_signatures: `if (pointer)` matches cmplwi while `if (pointer != NULL)` emits li plus cmplw
`while (*entry != 0)` is four bytes shorter than `while (*entry != NULL)`
the mismatch is isolated to null materialization and compare operands
integer 0 and 0L remain cmplwi while a consumer-local `(void *)addressHandle == NULL` produces li plus cmplw

patterns.rule: Run one bounded integer-zero versus pointer-null spelling control for an authenticated null guard. Retain the natural form only with exact text, branches, relocations, and consumers. Never cast opaque resource handles or change a public type merely to obtain the compare shape; a consumer-local cast is admissible only for an independently authenticated address-valued integer typedef whose target proves the pointer-domain comparison.
safe_actions: confirm the operand's pointer or address-handle semantics from headers and independent consumers
compare the emitted cmplwi versus li/cmplw sequence
preserve the target branch sense and null semantics

revert the spelling change if codegen is neutral or other instructions regress

Do not rewrite unrelated condition structure when only the null operand spelling differs.

patterns.title: Stop ordinary HuVecF copy spellings at a paired-single target
patterns.summary: Repeated GC/2.6 board evidence shows that a target HuVecF copy written with paired-single loads and stores is not reproduced by aggregate assignment, HuCopyVecF, memcpy, or a block-local pointer-mediated aggregate assignment: the two aggregate forms emit integer word copies, HuCopyVecF emits scalar float copies, and memcpy emits a call. These measured failures do not authenticate an intrinsic spelling.
patterns.conditions: Use only after target instructions prove a 12-byte HuVecF-shaped copy implemented with psq_l/psq_st plus the remaining scalar word, and after bounded controls for the applicable ordinary spellings have been measured under the pinned owner profile.

source_condition.change: Spell the same authenticated 12-byte vector transfer as direct or block-local pointer-mediated aggregate assignment, HuCopyVecF, or memcpy in an attempt to reproduce paired-single target instructions.
requires: target paired-single loads and stores for an authenticated HuVecF-shaped transfer
the pinned GC/2.6 owner command
strict function and relocation reports for each bounded spelling control
no authenticated intrinsic, helper, or historical header boundary already available

possible_changes: integer lwz/stw copies from aggregate assignment
the same integer lwz/stw copies after staging source and destination through block-local HuVecF pointers
an out-of-line memcpy call and a smaller but structurally wrong function
percentage movement without reproducing the target copy mechanism

block-local HuVecF pointers can change address-register and frame allocation while the dereferenced aggregate assignment still lowers to three integer-word loads and stores
HuCopyVecF preserves semantics but lowers to three scalar floating loads and stores
memcpy can improve one aggregate percentage while introducing a target-absent call
the ordinary non-solutions recur in separate board owners

If the applicable ordinary spellings retain the wrong mechanism, record the negative result and stop until an authenticated intrinsic, helper, compiler contract, or historical header boundary is found; do not guess paired-single intrinsics, add cast tricks, or use inline assembly.

retain strict size, score, instruction, and relocation results for each spelling
search authenticated same-game siblings and historical headers for the missing source boundary

patterns.title: Capture an authenticated owner pointer when its base must survive calls
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, a natural typed pointer to an authenticated global owner can keep one named base in a nonvolatile register across calls, while equivalent direct global field expressions may rematerialize the symbol and shorten or fragment the target address lifetime.
patterns.conditions: Use only when target instructions and relocations show one owner base surviving one or more calls, but the candidate repeatedly reloads the same authenticated global symbol or omits the target saved-base lifetime.

source_condition.change: Capture the authenticated global owner or array base in one natural typed pointer before its call-spanning uses.
requires: authenticated global identity, pointee type, and field or element ownership
target evidence for a call-spanning base lifetime or repeated candidate symbol reloads
unchanged control flow, call order, and consumer semantics
exact complete text and relocation stream after the bounded change

possible_changes: one named owner base retained in a callee-saved GPR
removal of repeated high/low symbol-address materialization
a matching nonvolatile-register save and restore lifetime
unchanged field offsets, calls, and owner identity
known_signatures: the candidate reloads one global symbol between calls while the target reuses a saved base
direct indexed access removes a target nonvolatile-register save
a typed local owner pointer closes both instruction and relocation differences without changing function size or control flow

patterns.rule: When an authenticated owner base visibly survives calls in the target, test one natural typed pointer capture at the first semantic use. Retain it only if complete text, saved-register lifetime, named relocations, and consumers become exact; if the target instead shortens the address lifetime, prefer direct access and record the counterexample.

compare high/low symbol relocations and nonvolatile-register saves before and after the probe
keep the pointer's scope no wider than the authenticated call-spanning lifetime

patterns.title: Prove downstream inline-consumer closure before extracting an exact cluster
patterns.summary: A source cluster can compile instruction- and relocation-exact in isolation yet be unsafe to bind as a new translation unit: moving its definitions can remove one-pass inline visibility from later callers that were already exact in the original combined source owner. A dependency-closed suffix, predecessor, or interior island can still be bound independently when every outgoing compile-time inline-consumer edge stays in the original translation unit and all protected consumers and pool owners remain exact. Function-address and callback assignments are link-only edges unless a direct compile-time call also exists.
patterns.conditions: Use when recovered functions are exact in a monolithic source owner and a proposed generated-object split moves their definitions into another translation unit while later exact callers remain behind.

source_condition.change: Extract an exact function cluster from a combined source owner into a separately compiled generated object.
requires: pinned compiler and flags for both the scratch and tracked objects
complete instruction and relocation equality for the extracted cluster
an inventory of every later independently exact caller whose compile-time visibility can change
before/after consumer-object comparison, not only extracted-object scoring
a dependency graph that identifies candidate regions with no compile-time visibility edge back into protected exact consumers
classification of direct-call inline-visibility edges separately from function-address or callback link-only edges

possible_changes: later callers replacing automatic inline expansions with calls
changed frames, saved-register lifetimes, and call relocations in untouched source bodies
a generated-object split regressing total exact coverage despite a perfect new object
known_signatures: scratch cluster text and relocations are exact but tracked owner-wide exact count falls
only consumers compiled after the moved definitions regress
restoring duplicate definitions would repair visibility but violate single-owner policy
later source references exist only as function-address assignments, so the moved body still links but no one-pass inline expansion can change

patterns.rule: Treat generated-object extraction as a consumer-closure change. Build a typed definition-to-consumer graph: direct compile-time calls to inline-capable definitions are visibility edges, while function-address and callback assignments are link-only edges unless a direct call also exists. Bind the cluster only when every affected exact caller remains exact or authenticated original header/TU evidence naturally preserves definition visibility; otherwise retain the exact C unbound and record the split as blocked.
safe_actions: enumerate later direct and transitive callers of every moved inline-capable definition
classify callback-address references separately and verify their final relocation targets without treating them as inline-visibility edges
compare all independently exact consumers after the tracked split
search target-contiguous prefixes, suffixes, and interior islands for the largest region with no outgoing definition-to-inline-consumer edge into retained exact code
expand the candidate owner boundary only when retail layout and source chronology authenticate it
revert the split rather than duplicate definitions or add pragmas and compiler controls

counterexamples: A split is safe when moved functions are not inline-capable at later exact call sites or every affected consumer remains instruction- and relocation-exact.
A perfect extracted-object score is not a counterexample unless the original owner and every previously exact consumer are also compared.
Do not preserve visibility with duplicate tracked definitions, forced-inline controls, pragmas, or fake storage.
A callback-address reference is not evidence of a compile-time inline edge; require a direct call or emitted inline expansion before expanding the closure.

patterns.title: Use an authenticated initialized local only for a target-proven O0 stack store
patterns.summary: A GC/2.6 -O0 function can retain an initialized scalar whose value is never referenced later, emitting a real prologue stack store while the function's working accumulator remains in a saved register. This is distinct from a declared-but-never-referenced local, which is codegen-neutral in the measured controls, and it is not permission to invent padding or dead storage.
patterns.conditions: Use only when an otherwise natural, exact-sized candidate has one unexplained target stack store to a bounded frame slot and authenticated same-game evidence supports an adjacent initialized scalar declaration.

source_condition.change: Test one naturally placed initialized scalar adjacent to the authenticated working locals.
requires: the pinned GC/2.6 -O0 owner command
raw target instructions and a target stack map
authenticated same-game source or consumer evidence for the scalar declaration
an otherwise exact control-flow and saved-register shape
strict text, relocation, neighbor-regression, and organicity checks

possible_changes: one immediate store to a real frame slot
no replacement of the saved-register-resident working accumulator
a shifted frame map if the declaration is placed in the wrong scope or chronology
known_signatures: the target has one unexplained li/stw zero initialization while the value used by later calls remains in a saved register
adding one adjacent initialized scalar closes the stack store without changing calls, branches, relocations, or exact neighbors
a merely declared never-referenced local emits no store and therefore cannot explain the target

patterns.rule: Treat an unexplained O0 stack store as declaration evidence only after target stack mapping and authenticated same-game evidence identify a plausible initialized scalar. Test one natural declaration and retain it only when complete text, relocations, consumers, and organicity become exact; never label it padding or generalize the result into a dead-local sweep.
safe_actions: map the target frame slot from raw PPC before editing source
use m2c stack output only as a hypothesis and replay it against raw instructions
test one authenticated declaration, initialization value, scope, and chronology at a time
require zero loss from the owner's existing exact-function set
revert immediately when the store, frame map, or semantic evidence does not close together
examples: main:board/capevent mbev_CapBonusCoinCall closed at 204/204 bytes and 8/8 relocations when one authenticated adjacent zero-initialized scalar reproduced the target stack store while coinNumWork remained saved-register resident.
counterexamples: A declared-but-never-referenced local is codegen-neutral in the measured controls and cannot explain an emitted store.
Do not add an initialized local solely because it improves match percentage when same-game evidence and the target frame map do not support it.
Do not use volatile, padding names, dummy arrays, fake reads, or dead branches to retain a store.
